 Bench At Aurangabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Mr.D.R.Kale, Public Prosecutor for the Respondent.

Coram : V.K.Jadhav, J.
 Date : 06th October, 2020.

Pc :
 1

The applicant is seeking bail in connection with Crime  No.0431/2020, registered with MIDC Waluj Police Station,
Aurangabad, for the ofences punishable under Sections 270, 273, 188, 328 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2 Heard both sides.

3 The learned Counsel for the applicant submits that the Police Head Constable on duty, during patrolling, found one auto rickshaw proceeding in speed in suspicious manner and thus he chased the said auto rickshaw.

Upon search, it was found that the contraband article pan gutkha masala,
costing {2} ba107620.odt about Rs.39,600/-, was being transported illegally.
The learned Counsel for the applicant submits that three co-accused persons, who were caught raid handed while transporting the said contraband article pan gutkha masala, came to be released on bail.

However,
one of the co-accused has disclosed the name of the applicant and it has been stated that they had Yogesh Vijay Katale vs The State Of Maharashtra on 6 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16981940/
1 purchased the said contraband article pan gutkha masala from the present applicant.

sentences.text: The learned Counsel submits that except the statement of the said co-accused person, which is not admissible in evidence, there is no connecting evidence against the applicant.
The applicant has a fxed place of residing.
The applicant is ready to abide by the conditions, if imposed by this Court, while releasing the applicant on bail.

4 The learned Public Prosecutor has strongly resisted the application on the ground that though the name of the applicant is disclosed by the co-accused person, however,
investigation is still going on.
The learned Public Prosecutor submits that there is criminal history.
One crime under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, came to be registered against the applicant.
The learned A.P.P., therefore, submits that the applicant may not be released on bail.

On going through the allegations made in the complaint and on perusal of the investigation papers, it appears that three co-accused persons, who were caught raid handed while transporting the contraband article pan gutkha masala, came to be released on bail.
However, the applicant came to be arrested on the basis of disclosure statement made by one of the co-accused person.
Except the said disclosure statement of one of the co-accused person, which is not admissible in evidence, there is no connecting evidence against the applicant.
There is only one crime registered against the applicant, which is identical to the present crime.
6 Considering the entire aspects of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail on certain conditions.

7 Hence, the following order:
 (I) Application is hereby allowed.

(ii) The applicant Yogsh Vijay Katale, in connection with Crime No. 0431/2020, registered with MIDC Waluj Police Station, Aurangabad, for the ofences punishable under Sections 270, 273, 188, 328 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, be {4}
ba107620.odt released on bail on furnishing Personal Bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rs. Twenty Thousand)
with one solvent surety in the like amount, on the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution, evidence in any manner.
(b) The applicant shall attend the concerned Police Station once in a week i.e. on every Sunday between 08.00 a.m. to 11.00 p.m. till the fling of charge sheet.
8 Application is accordingly disposed of.

(V.K.JADHAV) JUDGE adb Yogesh Vijay Katale vs The State Of Maharashtra on 6 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16981940/
